title: Rosette Nebula Captured with DECam
caption: The Rosette Nebula and star cluster NGC 2244, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
celestial: NGC 2244 · constellation Monoceros · about 5000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA. Image Processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), D. de Martin & M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Red, gold and purple clouds billow around a hollowed-out centre in this view of the Rosette Nebula, with opaque towers of dust rising from the gas. In that cleared core sits NGC 2244, the young star cluster the nebula gave birth to, whose stars now light it up. The nebula lies about 5000 light-years away in Monoceros.

The Rosette is an emission nebula, a cloud of gas that glows because hot young stars nearby pour energetic light into it. The members of a cluster like NGC 2244 are born from the same cloud they later illuminate, and their radiation and winds gradually push the surrounding gas away, which is how a cavity like this one can be carved out.

The dark towers are denser pockets of dust and gas that hold out against that erosion for longer. The picture was taken with the 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and released to mark NOIRLab's fifth anniversary.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (94.75 x 80.62 arcminutes) and distance (5000 light years), the frame spans roughly 138 × 117 light-years. Its light set out about 5,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through narrow filters for sulfur (S II), oxygen (O III) and hydrogen-alpha. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
filters: 673 nm · Optical S II (NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope DECam)
501 nm · Optical OIII (NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope DECam)
662 nm · Optical H-alpha (NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope DECam)
understand.eye: The narrow filters isolate glows from particular gases, and long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the colours are much richer than a telescope view would show.

explore: DECam was fabricated by the US Department of Energy and is mounted on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, which stands at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory. NOIRLab's Communication, Education & Engagement team produced the image for its Legacy Imaging Program.
